$comment: QAE reason-code registry (DRAFT). Closed set; adding a code is a versioned change. Codes are never UI strings — hosts map them to Arabic/English copy in the app i18n layer. severity: info | notice | warning | safety.

codes.description: Trend within the goal's target band; plan kept.
Weight trend stable across the required evidence window with verified intake adherence.
Calorie and training adherence above thresholds with sufficient confidence.
Adherence below threshold; adaptation deferred in favor of adherence support.
Insufficient logging to verify adherence; no adaptation on unverified data.
Two or more recovery markers trending negative with sufficient confidence.
A goal-progress calorie reduction was suppressed by recovery-class rules.
Evidence gates unmet; requesting more data instead of adapting.
Observed loss rate above the safe band for the population (EVR-001).
Observed gain rate above the lean-gain band (EVR-010).
Step target met across the exposure period; increase eligible.
Step increase withheld: recovery poor, volume just increased, or calories substantially reduced.
Intake consistently above target; adherence-support path engaged, never punitive.
Weight-modification goals unavailable under 18; maintenance applied (characterized live policy).
Age unknown; assessment cannot finalize (supersedes legacy L-SAF-1 default-adult).
Age below the app minimum (13); no plan issuable (characterized live policy).
Calorie target clamped to the safety floor; clamp visible by design.
Requested target in VLCD territory (<800 kcal, EVR-009); not issuable.
Volume increase outside the ValidDecisionSpace under recovery decline.
A composite bundle carried a non-protective component; rejected (DECISION-MODEL §3.3).
Exercises excluded via contraindication metadata for reported injury flags.
Filters left a day underfilled; named signal (supersedes silent legacy underfill L-TRN-4).
Screening flags require professional clearance; engine offers safe fallback only. Never a diagnosis.
Sustained arrival at goal target; transition recommended, requires confirmation.
Long uninterrupted deficit with fatigue/hunger markers; transition or break recommended.
Goal transition recommended for safety; decision space bounded meanwhile.
New goal instance started on explicit user request.
Re-entry ramp in effect; workload below knowledge-implied level.
Reassurance: retraining gains outpace initial gains (EVR-014). Messaging only.
Fasting context supplied by host; context-aware baselines in effect.
Trend comparisons suppressed across a context/goal-phase boundary.
Eating/drinking window compressed; host may show hydration guidance copy. No prescriptions.
Variable changed recently or proposal recently rejected; change deferred.
The cycle's major-change slot is used; remaining candidates deferred.
Same (variable, direction) was rejected recently; the engine does not re-nag (fixture S30).
Manual and device sources disagree for the same day; precedence applied, both retained.
An implausible reading was down-weighted in trend fitting; visible in the quality report.
Reading outside physical bounds; excluded, visibly.
Readings older than the staleness window excluded from current-state reads.
No usable data for the period; requesting data, adapting nothing (fixture S33).
Training performance markers trending down with sufficient confidence.
First-week workload reduced for a safe start (characterized legacy behavior).
Beginner with ≥5 requested days; lower frequency advised (characterized).
Chosen split trains legs fewer than 2×/week (characterized; EVR-004).
Targets computed with the averaged sex constant; estimates approximate (characterized).
Recovery-management deload proposed; optional, practice-based (EVR-010).
Progression paused as a protective component.
No rule fired this cycle; keepPlan emitted with the strongest not-fired reasons attached.
A rule's declarative preconditions evaluated false; recorded in the trace as a named non-firing.
Candidate lost same-variable conflict resolution to a higher-priority rule; recorded with the suppressor.
